hosts.name: win-vuln-dc
hosts.title: win-vuln-dc (2012 R2 DC): EternalBlue + KEV Sept 2026 rollup
hosts.priority: P1 / Emergency (Tier 1 CISA KEV, unauthenticated network RCE on a domain controller)
summary: win-vuln-dc is a domain controller still missing MS17-010 (EternalBlue), a wormable
SMBv1 remote-code-execution flaw used by WannaCry and NotPetya, plus the CISA KEV-listed
September 2026 rollup. Code execution on a domain controller means full compromise of
the domain. Its kernel (ntoskrnl 6.3.9600.17041) is essentially unpatched since 2014.
Windows Server 2012 R2 extended security updates end 13 Oct 2026, so this may be one
of the last patches available; migration must be planned separately.
change: One maintenance window, one reboot:
1. Tenable (plugin 343860): "Apply Security Update 5123066".
Target: C:\Windows\system32\ntoskrnl.exe at 6.3.9600.23398 (currently 6.3.9600.17041).
2. Tenable (plugin 97737): "Microsoft has released a set of patches for ... 2012 R2 ...";
missing rollup KB4012213 or KB4012216; win32k.sys should be 6.3.9600.18603.
KB5123066 is a later monthly rollup and should supersede these. Confirm with the rescan;
if 97737 still fires, apply KB4012213 directly.
3. Reboot. If another DC is available, confirm replication health before and after
(repadmin /replsummary).
interim: (Own note, not Tenable text.)
- Disable SMBv1 now, before the window: Set-SmbServerConfiguration -EnableSMB1Protocol $false
- Restrict TCP 445 to this DC from management and member-server subnets only.
risk: EternalBlue gives an unauthenticated attacker SYSTEM on the DC over the network (lateral
movement T1210), which is a direct path to domain admin. This is priority #2 in the
briefing (score 0.81); with #1 it closes 18 of the 42 KEV host/plugin pairs (43%).

hosts.name: water-plant-02
hosts.title: water-plant-02: ScreenConnect 19.2 (3 KEV flaws) + Office Equation Editor
hosts.priority: P1 / Emergency (Tier 1 CISA KEV, unauthenticated RCE, ransomware-linked)
summary: This host runs ConnectWise ScreenConnect 19.2, which has three CISA KEV-listed flaws.
CVE-2024-1709/1708 together give an outside attacker remote code execution with no
login and were used by LockBit and Black Basta. CVE-2026-84869 lets files be transferred
and run through a session without authorization, and CISA reports it exploited in the
wild since September 2026.
water-plant-02 is likely operational-technology equipment (inferred from hostname) and
also has the unpatched Office Equation Editor flaw, a common phishing entry point.
Both fixes fit one window.
change: 1. Tenable (plugin 344805): "Upgrade to ConnectWise ScreenConnect version 26.6.5 or later."
Path: C:\Program Files (x86)\ScreenConnect\Bin\  Installed: 19.2.29494.7513
Go straight to 26.6.5 or later. Plugin 190886's target of 23.9.8 is NOT enough:
it leaves CVE-2026-84869 (KEV) open.
2. Tenable (plugin 104557): "Microsoft has released security updates for Microsoft
Office Products." Apply KB4011262 for Office 2016.
Target: C:\Program Files\Common Files\Microsoft Shared\Equation\eqnedt32.exe
interim: (Own note, not Tenable text.)
- Stop and disable the ScreenConnect client service until upgraded, or block the host's
outbound connection to the ScreenConnect relay at the firewall.
- Hunt before patching: unexpected ScreenConnect sessions or admin users, and wscript.exe
or .vbs files launched by the ScreenConnect client (TTP reported by Huntress).
- Disable Equation Editor: set "Compatibility Flags"=dword:00000400 under
HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Office\Common\COM Compatibility\{0002CE02-0000-0000-C000-000000000046}
rollback: - Take a VM snapshot or backup before the upgrade.
- Rolling back to 19.2 reopens all three KEV flaws; if 26.6.5 breaks support
workflows, leave the client disabled rather than reinstalling 19.2.
risk: ScreenConnect is remote-access software, so exploitation gives an attacker hands-on
control (Initial Access T1190/T1133). This is priority #3 in the briefing (score 0.75);
the five upgrades close 10 of the 42 KEV host/plugin pairs (24%).

hosts.title: rita-lpt: ScreenConnect 19.2 (3 KEV flaws)
hosts.priority: P1 / Emergency (Tier 1 CISA KEV, unauthenticated RCE, ransomware-linked)
summary: This host runs ConnectWise ScreenConnect 19.2, which has three CISA KEV-listed flaws.
CVE-2024-1709/1708 together give an outside attacker remote code execution with no
login and were used by LockBit and Black Basta. CVE-2026-84869 lets files be transferred
and run through a session without authorization, and CISA reports it exploited in the
wild since September 2026.
change: 1. Tenable (plugin 344805): "Upgrade to ConnectWise ScreenConnect version 26.6.5 or later."
Path: C:\Program Files (x86)\ScreenConnect\Bin\  Installed: 19.2.29494.7513
Go straight to 26.6.5 or later. Plugin 190886's target of 23.9.8 is NOT enough:
it leaves CVE-2026-84869 (KEV) open.
interim: (Own note, not Tenable text.)
- Stop and disable the ScreenConnect client service until upgraded, or block the host's
outbound connection to the ScreenConnect relay at the firewall.
- Hunt before patching: unexpected ScreenConnect sessions or admin users, and wscript.exe
or .vbs files launched by the ScreenConnect client (TTP reported by Huntress).
rollback: - Take a VM snapshot or backup before the upgrade.
- Rolling back to 19.2 reopens all three KEV flaws; if 26.6.5 breaks support
workflows, leave the client disabled rather than reinstalling 19.2.
risk: ScreenConnect is remote-access software, so exploitation gives an attacker hands-on
control (Initial Access T1190/T1133). This is priority #3 in the briefing (score 0.75);
the five upgrades close 10 of the 42 KEV host/plugin pairs (24%).
